title: Finding a Little Inner Calm
summary: From restless to settled: a gentle meditation for a busy mind.
script:
Hi there! Today's meditation is “Finding a Little Inner Calm”.
Take a moment to get comfortable.
You might have had a busy day, a long morning, or maybe you’re just looking for a little time to yourself. Whatever brought you here, you don’t need to change anything right now.
Just let yourself settle.
You can close your eyes if that feels comfortable, or keep them open if you prefer.
For the next few minutes, there’s nowhere else you need to be.
Just take a breath, slow things down, and be here for a while.
Let's begin.
I want you to check in for a moment. Notice your body, right now, exactly as it is. Not judging it, just noticing.
Is there a little tension anywhere? A slight tightness in your jaw, maybe? A mind that keeps jumping from one thing to the next, unable to fully land on anything.
If you're noticing any of that, that's what we'd call feeling restless. Restless means your body or mind can't quite calm down, it keeps moving, searching for something, even when there's nowhere it actually needs to go. Think of it like a bird that keeps hopping from branch to branch, never quite landing anywhere long enough to rest.
Notice, gently, if there is a little restlessness in you right now.
Restlessness is the noun, the feeling itself.
Restless is the adjective, it describes how you feel.
You don’t need to fix it or make it go away. Just notice it’s there.
Inhale slowly.
Restlessness isn't wrong, by the way. It's just energy. Most of us carry a little of it, most days, especially after a long day, or a busy one. A busy day at work, for example.
Exhale slowly.
Let’s give that energy a moment to slow down.
Bring your attention to your feet, wherever they are right now. Notice them, simply resting, touching the floor, or the bed. They're not going anywhere. They don't need to move.
Breathe in slowly, and imagine your feet becoming a little heavier.
Breathe out, and let that feeling move gently into your legs. Let your legs become a little heavier.
Notice how this feels different from the busy feeling you felt before.
You don’t need to think about what comes next. Just notice your body here, feeling calm, heavy, and still.
Inhale again.
Yeah, so this feeling has a name too, and the name is settled. Settled means your body and mind have finally stopped searching, and simply rested into where they already are. Think of it like the same bird from earlier, finally choosing one branch, and staying there, quiet, and still, relaxed.
Exhale slowly.
Let this settled feeling continue spreading. Spreading from your legs, up into your stomach, your chest. Notice your breath, still moving, but slower now, calmer, with nowhere urgent to be.
Inhale, feeling this quiet weight rest in your chest.
Exhale, releasing anything that still feels restless, anything still searching for something else.
Notice your shoulders now. Let them drop a little further, settling completely, the way that bird's wings finally fold, once it's found its branch.
Inhale slowly.
And your hands, wherever they're resting right now. Let them be heavy, and still. Nothing left to hold onto, nothing left to search for.
Exhale completely.
Notice how your mind feels right now, too.
It might still be a little busy, and that’s okay. Maybe it feels a little quieter than before, even if only a little. That’s also okay.
You don’t need to force yourself to feel calm. You are not trying to stop feeling restless forever. You’re simply practicing landing here, in this present moment.
When we say “landing,” we mean arriving and becoming settled in a place or moment. We use this word for planes when they arrive on the ground, but we can also use it when we talk about meditation.
For these few minutes, you’re simply giving yourself time to arrive here, to land here, and be still.
Inhale.
And exhale, long, and slow.
Now, a few words, if you'd like to hold onto them.
I don't need to search for anything right now.
I don't need to search for anything right now.
I am allowed to settle, exactly where I am.
I am allowed to settle, exactly where I am.
Restlessness can visit, and it can also leave.
Restlessness can visit, and it can also leave.
My body knows how to rest, even when my mind is busy.
My body knows how to rest, even when my mind is busy.
I am settling, a little more, with every breath.
I am settling, a little more, with every breath.
Take one more slow breath in.
And breathe out, completely.
You can stay here for a little longer if you’d like. You can take a few moments to notice how your body feels.
And when you’re ready to come back, start noticing what is around you.
Feel the chair, floor, or bed supporting your body.
Notice any sounds you can hear.
Then notice your breathing, slow and easy.
Gently move your fingers.
Then move your feet.
And whenever you’re ready, slowly open your eyes.

vocabulary.definition: when your body or mind can’t quite calm down and keeps moving, searching for something
when your body and mind have stopped searching and simply rest where they are
